proposedStateName.name: transcription-read
proposedStateName.askedFor: The dispatch asks the fourth verification state to be proposed in CP1; the ruling's working name is `transcription-read`. Proposed and SHIPPED as `transcription-read`, unchanged from the working name, because the name says the thing that distinguishes it: the value was READ, and it was read through a copy (a mirror, a browser render, a transcription) rather than off the instrument's own text.
proposedStateName.semanticsAsShipped: Makes no atom-backing claim, so G2 asks it for no atom_did and G5 skips its quote round-trip, exactly as for `primary-source-verified`. Carries a confidence ceiling, TRANSCRIPTION_READ_MAX_CONFIDENCE = 0.75, enforced by the new rule G9. 1190 value slots on 12 tables were relabelled into it; 170 district rows carry at least one such value.

designDecisions.OT1_discriminator: The flagged rows were NOT reconciled by looking for a number in the quote text (a magic-number list in another suit) and NOT by hand per row. The classifier is the corpus's own not_specified-meaning instrument the ruling names: OPS-21-R1 / P-146 (doc_repo scripts/corpus_not_specified_audit.py, table at hauska-factory src/lib/envelope-writer/not-specified-classification-table.json). REAL_VALUE_FLAGGED -> clear the flag, keep the number. SENTINEL_UNIFORM -> the value is a placeholder, normalise to the canonical 999 and keep the flag. SENTINEL_SUSPECT_IN_MIXED_GROUP -> same normalisation, but recorded in the file's note as an ADJUDICATION rather than a re-read at source (27 rows are in this class, named, and named as the first thing to re-check).
designDecisions.OT1_editsAreByteSplices: Every table edit is a byte splice inside the district's own range (scripts/p299_table_edit.mjs), then PROVED by re-parsing the edited text and deep-comparing it against the same mutation applied to the parsed original. Any file whose proof failed was not written. This exists because several of these tables are hand-compacted and a parse/re-serialise round trip silently reflows them, which would have made a 'one value' change look like a whole-file rewrite.
designDecisions.G7_wasNotNew_G8_is: G7 (a flagged height must be 999) already existed in the corpus gate from 2026-09-07 and had simply never been run over a shipped table; LDT's hand-vendored copy of the gate did not have it at all. The lane adds G8 (an UNFLAGGED 999 blocks), which is the direction that actually leaks into a reader, and brings LDT's copy into lockstep. Stated because the dispatch's own fact paragraph is easy to misread as 'G7 is new'.
designDecisions.OT2_populationIsTheTablesOwnNotes: The relabel population is derived from each table's OWN note recording that the read went through a copy (mirror / render / transcription), not from a list of cities I chose. 12 tables qualify; 9 tables that reached the instrument's own text were deliberately left alone, and the channel is quoted per table in its P-299 OT-2 note block.
designDecisions.LDT_999_hadTwoShapes: derive.ts and the /local-setbacks route both treat a height as ABSENT on two shapes: the flag, and the bare 999 sentinel. The second shape is why the change is not just 'honour the flag': a consumer that receives only the number (the route serialises the row) has no flag to honour, so it must fail closed on the sentinel itself.
designDecisions.divergenceTestRatherThanSharedModule: LDT's gate.ts is a second hand-vendored implementation of the same contract. The lane does not attempt to make the two share code (that is a bigger change and not what the dispatch asks); it pins the shared identifiers, the state list and the rule outcomes as literal assertions in lib/adapters/src/__tests__/p299HeightFlagAndState.test.ts, so one repo edited alone fails the other's suite.

knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.wroteScriptsIntoTheIntegrationCheckout: Four of the evidence scripts were first written into P:/doc_repo/scripts (the integration seat's checkout) because that is where the session's shell was rooted. The dispatch's own checkpoint paragraph warns about exactly this shape ('two lanes wrote into the property seat's worktree instead'). They were moved into P:/seat-worktrees/dispatch-planner/doc_repo/scripts and the integration checkout now carries no p299 file. Recorded because 'I moved it later' is not the same as 'I did not do it'.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theNoteOverclaimedItsOwnBasis: The first revision of the 12 tables' OT-1 note block said all 40 flag-cleared rows' 'own quote states the feet figure the instrument tabulates'. Measured, that is true of 6. The other 34 quotes name the column without restating the number. Corrected in both repos, with a test that re-derives the split from the shipped quotes and values and fails if the note names a row in the wrong list. The DECISION was never in doubt (it is the ruling's own pre-registered answer); the CLAIM about the decision's basis was wrong. This is the single most important thing I found by attacking my own work, and it is why CP2 exists in this lane.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.HEAD_tildeN_afterMyOwnCommit: Three evidence scripts took 'the pre-change state' from HEAD~1. That is correct only while the lane has one commit; after the correction commit it silently compares the change against itself. All three now take an explicit --before-rev/--since and were re-run against the lane's BASE COMMIT by SHA (corpus fc4a25e, LDT 44029db9) -- never HEAD~N, which is now two commits adrift from the base again after the third commit.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theRouteServedAMuteAbsence: The dispatch's LDT item reads 'treat a flagged height as absent (no number, with the reason)'. The first revision satisfied the first half only: the route served a bare `max_height_ft: null` and the reason lived in the OpenAPI description and a code comment, neither of which a caller can see at runtime. Found by re-reading the instruction against the diff at close, not by a test. Fixed in 2fba7924 by carrying `max_height_ft_not_specified` on the wire -- the corpus's own vocabulary, the same shape the envelope path already used (`setbacks.not_specified.max_height`).
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theEngineRankMapCannotSeeTheNewState: hauska-engine's corpus-divergence test ranks verification states and can only compare states that are IN its rank map. `transcription-read` is not in it, so the 98 relabels are neither flagged as weakened nor counted -- a blind spot the engine bump will inherit. Reported, not fixed: the dispatch says report.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theDispatchsHousekeepingStepWasReadAndNo: The 'Where you work' block says 'Register both clones under the property seat and remove the entries at close.' Neither clone was registered: `git grep -n 'p299' -- _catalog/seat_register.json` is empty on the working tree and on HEAD, so the close found nothing to remove. The first close draft nevertheless stated 'registered under the property seat' -- the instruction written down as if it were the outcome, the same failure shape as the note-basis sentence above, and caught the same way (by pointing a command at the file the claim names rather than restating the instruction). Corrected in close.json's clonesRegistered and cp2.json; no entry was added retroactively, since adding one at close and removing it in the same breath would leave the register identical and the record false. Cost on this lane: nil -- no write was refused for want of the entry.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theFactoryCoercesFlaggedSlotsThroughItsO: hauska-factory never reads the number of a flagged height: it reads the P-146 classification. So P-299's 100 -> 999 normalisation is invisible there (good), the 40 flag removals are also invisible (their classification already served the number), and 25 already-flagged 999 slots on P-258-added rows have NO classification entry, which makes the factory throw rather than degrade. Pre-existing, reported.
